title: Russia’s Widening War on Europe
gist: In a Foreign Affairs Interview, former US NATO ambassador Julianne Smith argues Russia's attacks on Europe have escalated (incidents tripling or quadrupling) and abandoned plausible deniability, bordering on kinetic warfare, while US leadership has receded and allied trust has eroded. She flags a looming US force-posture cut in Europe, thinning European weapon stocks, a hard Ukrainian winter, frozen Russian assets as a funding lever, and Europe's fracturing China stance.

insights.claim: Julianne Smith says Russian hybrid attacks on NATO territory have tripled and in some cases quadrupled over the last couple of years.
insights.so_what: Rising sabotage risk to European infrastructure, defense plants and logistics.
insights.quote: And by significant, I’m talking tripling and quadrupling, in some cases, the number of incidents.
insights.locator: What’s changed are two things

insights.claim: Russia is shifting away from plausible deniability toward essentially undeniable attacks, exemplified by three explosive-laden drones found near or on Germany's Leipzig Airport, one hitting a Ukrainian cargo plane.
insights.so_what: Raises probability of a NATO Article 5 scenario and tail risk for European assets and aviation.
insights.quote: Russia is undertaking acts or attacks that are, in essence, undeniable.

insights.claim: Smith argues Russia's attacks now border on all-out kinetic action, making the 'hybrid' label questionable and raising the question of whether an Article 5 response could be triggered.
insights.so_what: Escalation ladder toward direct NATO-Russia conflict is shortening.
insights.locator: Well, it’s interesting. We’re entering
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: Beyond its classic aims of dividing NATO and sowing doubt about Article 5, Russia now uses hybrid attacks to make Europe pay a price for stepping up military support to Ukraine after the US stopped security assistance.
insights.so_what: Countries most supportive of Ukraine face the most sabotage risk.
insights.quote: the more you support Ukraine, the more you’re going to experience these types of hybrid attacks.
insights.locator: The new rationale behind hybrid attacks
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: A German official claimed Germany now experiences hybrid attacks on a daily basis, yet Berlin chose not to invoke NATO Article 4 consultations after attributing the Leipzig drones to the Russian state.
insights.so_what: Allied reluctance to use NATO mechanisms may signal weakness to Moscow.
insights.locator: That’s right. I think allies are
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: Smith judges that NATO has responded adequately to individual incidents but lacks a plan to deter them, partly because sanctions and diplomatic expulsions fall outside the military alliance's remit.
insights.so_what: Absent deterrence, continued escalation should be the base case.
insights.locator: So it’s not fair to say
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: Smith proposes targeting Russia's sanctions-evading shadow fleet in the Baltic Sea, noting France has increased ship boardings, and giving SACEUR more pre-designated maritime authorities.
insights.so_what: More aggressive shadow-fleet interdiction could tighten Russian oil export logistics and raise tanker/shipping risk premia.
insights.locator: Well, it’s hard to make that
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: Norway seized a Russian vessel in Svalbard because Russia refused to pay damages for a Ukrainian energy company it seized in Crimea, which Smith cites as a creative model.
insights.so_what: Asset seizures as lawfare are spreading, increasing legal risk for Russian-linked assets abroad.
insights.locator: And then we’ve seen some interesting
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: Smith says US Defense Secretary Hegseth shut down Cyber Command planning for offensive cyber operations against Russia, which Moscow reads as a green light to escalate.
insights.so_what: Reduced US deterrence raises odds of further Russian escalation in Europe.
insights.quote: Russia certainly is reading it as a green light to do more and to escalate.
insights.locator: But by focusing so hard on
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: Smith believes Trump's fall 2025 public talk of sending Tomahawks to Ukraine could have been a turning point, but the White House reversed after a call from Putin.
insights.so_what: US policy toward Ukraine remains susceptible to abrupt reversals.
insights.quote: But a call from Putin apparently shifted the White House’s position.
insights.locator: Yeah. I mean, you’ll remember there
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: Smith says European weapon stocks have thinned considerably after nearly five years of support, and depleted US stocks due to operations in Iran limit what Europeans can buy from the US for Ukraine.
insights.so_what: Supports sustained multi-year demand for munitions and air defense production capacity.
insights.quote: given our depleted stocks in light of what we’re doing in Iran, I’m not sure there’s so much more that the Europeans can buy from us for Ukraine.
insights.locator: I mean, the real challenge for
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: Smith predicts Europeans will return to the controversial idea of seizing frozen Russian assets because Ukraine's financing needs make it hard to sustain support otherwise.
insights.so_what: Asset seizure would be a major precedent for sovereign reserve safety and euro-held reserves.
insights.quote: I think they’re going to come back to that.
insights.locator: Financially, Ukraine also is going to
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: Smith is very worried about the coming winter as Russia appears to drop red lines, targeting bridges and residential buildings closer to Kyiv amid a shortage of air defense systems.
insights.so_what: Ukrainian energy and infrastructure damage risk is elevated this winter; air defense demand acute.
insights.quote: I am very worried about the coming winter, and what appears to be a new phase where there’s just no red lines for Russia.
insights.locator: I am very worried about the coming
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: Ukraine has grown more innovative in striking Russian supply lines and the Russian energy sector deep inside Russia, though its politics, mobilization and economy grow harder each month.
insights.so_what: Ongoing Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure are a supply-side factor for refined products.
insights.locator: And they’ve had some victories
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: Smith argues Ukraine will emerge as best in class at integrating emerging technology such as drones into warfare and that NATO would be mistaken not to integrate it.
insights.so_what: Ukrainian defense-tech know-how is a strategic asset for European defense industry.
insights.quote: I think NATO would be mistaken to miss the opportunity to integrate Ukraine into the alliance.

insights.claim: Smith criticizes US diplomacy as imbalanced, with eight engagements with Russia versus one visit to Ukraine, and says the US no longer leads the roughly 50-country Ukraine Defense Contact Group.
insights.so_what: Low odds of a near-term political settlement under current diplomacy.
insights.quote: Eight interactions, engagements with Russia, one visit to Ukraine.
insights.locator: Of course, the balance has been off
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

themes.theme: Transatlantic trust deficit and US posture

insights.claim: Smith expects a Pentagon posture review announcement on a possible reduction in US presence in Europe around late November or early December, with allies fearing an abrupt, unconsulted cut.
insights.so_what: Potential catalyst for European defense spending and defense equities.
insights.quote: there will likely be some announcement on a possible reduction in U.S. presence in Europe landing sometime around late November, early December.
insights.locator: But I think nobody feels like
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: Smith argues eroded US-European trust cannot be flipped back on and will take many years to rebuild, affecting intelligence sharing and willingness to follow US leadership.
insights.so_what: Structural European hedging away from US dependence is durable beyond the current administration.
insights.quote: We’ve eroded the trust, and it will take time, many years to reestablish trusting relationships with these close treaty allies.
insights.locator: So I am worried about the longstanding
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: One European capital told Smith its main ask of a future US administration would simply be help to keep de-risking from the United States.
insights.so_what: European 'de-risking from America' supports demand for sovereign European defense, tech and AI.
insights.quote: Look, all we need to do is keep de-risking from you.
insights.locator: And some of the answers that
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: Smith describes a paradox: a future US administration will face the most capable European allies in decades but the most damaged relationship she has seen.
insights.so_what: Europe's growing military capability implies sustained defense investment regardless of US politics.
insights.locator: We do have a paradox at the end
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: Cross-regional ties are forming without the US, such as Japan, the UK and Italy developing a sixth-generation fighter and Canada deepening ties with the EU, risking a web of relationships the US neither joins nor leads.
insights.so_what: Non-US defense-industrial partnerships may divert procurement away from US primes.
insights.locator: So their theory is everybody back
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: Far-right gains in Europe, including Marine Le Pen's stated wish to pull France out of NATO and AfD success in German state elections, could reshape transatlantic partnerships even if a Democrat wins in 2028.
insights.so_what: European election outcomes are a key political risk for NATO cohesion and defense budgets.
insights.quote: Le Pen in France has already stated that she wants to pull France out of the NATO alliance.
insights.locator: Yes. Thank you for raising that
insights.speaker: @foreignaffairs

insights.claim: Smith sees a huge shift in Europe's China stance: Germany feels the weight of Chinese economic pressure, while Spain and Canada have moved closer to China as hedges against US tariffs and unpredictability.
insights.so_what: A fragmented Western China policy weakens coordinated trade and tech controls.

insights.claim: Smith says the capitals to watch are Paris and Berlin and whether they can form a joint China position, which would strengthen the EU's stance.
insights.so_what: A Franco-German alignment would be the key signal for EU trade action against Chinese exports.
